questions.stem: Petrol in a drip tray catches fire while an apprentice is draining a tank. The apprentice reaches for a bucket. Why should he be stopped if the bucket holds water?
options: Water would cool the fire too quickly
Water makes petrol explode like gunpowder
Petrol floats on water, so the fire would spread
Water is needed later for the radiator
Water has no effect on any kind of fire
questions.explanation: Petrol floats on water, so the burning liquid would be carried further; foam, powder, CO2 or dry sand should be used.

questions.stem: Of the following, which is the SAFEST way to support a car for a gearbox removal job lasting two hours?
options: leave the engine idling in gear
rely on the jack alone as long as it is new
deflate the tyres a little for stability
remove the wheels on the other side as well
On axle stands at the correct jacking points
questions.explanation: A jack can sink or fail; the vehicle must rest on axle stands before anyone goes under it.

questions.stem: The instrument best suited to measuring the diameter of a crankshaft journal to 0.01 mm is the
questions.explanation: An outside micrometer reads to 0.01 mm and is used for journal and piston diameters.

questions.stem: A torque wrench is used when tightening cylinder head bolts in order to
options: tighten all bolts as hard as possible
speed up the work with power assistance
questions.explanation: Head bolts must be tightened to a specified torque in sequence to avoid distortion and gasket failure.

questions.stem: In a front-engine rear-wheel-drive car, power reaches the rear axle through the
questions.explanation: The propeller shaft carries drive from the gearbox at the front to the final drive at the rear.

questions.stem: Which drive arrangement does NOT need a propeller shaft running along the length of the car?
options: Front engine driving a rear axle lorry
questions.explanation: In front-wheel drive, engine, gearbox and final drive are grouped at the front and drive shafts go straight to the front wheels.

questions.stem: In a four-stroke petrol engine, both valves are closed and the piston moves up during the
questions.explanation: On compression, both valves are shut while the piston compresses the charge.

questions.stem: A four-cylinder engine of total capacity 1600 cm³ is to have a compression ratio of 9 : 1. The clearance volume of EACH cylinder must be
questions.explanation: Swept volume per cylinder = 400 cm³; CR = (Vs + Vc)/Vc gives Vc = Vs/(CR - 1) = 400/8 = 50 cm³.

questions.stem: The usual firing order of a four-cylinder in-line engine is
questions.explanation: 1-3-4-2 (or 1-2-4-3 on some) is used; 1-3-4-2 is the most common and balances loads along the crankshaft.

questions.stem: The inlet valve opens 12° before TDC and closes 48° after BDC. For how many degrees of crankshaft rotation is the inlet valve open?
In the same engine the exhaust valve closes 16° after TDC. The valve overlap is
questions.explanation: Overlap = inlet opening before TDC + exhaust closing after TDC = 12 + 16 = 28°.

questions.stem: Roughly how many kilograms of air are needed to burn 2 kg of petrol completely?
questions.explanation: The correct air-fuel ratio is about 14.7 : 1 by mass, so 2 kg of petrol needs about 29.4 kg of air.

questions.stem: Black smoke from the exhaust of a petrol car usually indicates
questions.explanation: Excess fuel burns incompletely and produces carbon (soot), giving black smoke; blue smoke indicates oil burning.

questions.stem: Air that has entered the fuel lines of a diesel engine after the tank ran dry is removed by
questions.explanation: Bleeding at the filter, pump and injector unions expels air, which would otherwise stop injection.

questions.stem: The main purpose of the silencer is to
questions.explanation: The silencer (muffler) reduces gas pressure pulses and so lowers exhaust noise.

questions.stem: In a forced-feed lubrication system, oil is delivered to the main bearings by
questions.explanation: A gear or rotor pump driven by the engine forces oil through galleries to the bearings.

questions.stem: An oil marked SAE 20W-50 is
options: a single-grade oil for gearboxes only
an oil with no viscosity rating
questions.explanation: The W grade gives cold viscosity and the second number gives hot viscosity; it is a multigrade.

questions.stem: In a two-stroke "petroil" engine, the crankshaft bearings are lubricated by
options: a pressure pump from the gearbox
questions.explanation: Oil is premixed with petrol; it lubricates the crankcase parts as the mixture passes through.

questions.stem: The cooling system thermostat stays closed when the engine is cold in order to
options: stop the radiator from leaking at the hose joints
help the engine warm up fast
questions.explanation: With the thermostat closed, coolant does not pass through the radiator, so the engine reaches working temperature quickly.

questions.stem: Pressurising the cooling system with a radiator cap raises the
questions.explanation: Higher pressure raises the boiling point, so the engine can run hotter without the coolant boiling.

questions.stem: Compared with water cooling, air cooling has the ADVANTAGE that it
options: has no coolant to leak or boil
allows larger engines to be cooled easily
questions.explanation: Air-cooled engines have no radiator, hoses or pump, so there is nothing to leak or boil, though they are noisier.

questions.stem: The clutch allows the driver to
options: disconnect the engine from the gearbox
questions.explanation: Disengaging the clutch separates the engine drive so gears can be changed or the car can stop with the engine running.

questions.stem: An engine produces 180 N m. Its single-plate clutch (two friction faces) has a mean lining radius of 0.12 m and μ = 0.25. The least total spring force that will stop the clutch slipping is
In a gearbox the constant-mesh pair has 20 and 40 teeth and second gear pair has 25 (layshaft) and 30 (mainshaft) teeth. The second gear ratio is
The differential in the rear axle is needed because
options: outer wheels travel further on bends
questions.explanation: On a bend the outer wheel must turn faster; the differential allows this while still driving both wheels.

questions.stem: In the tyre marking 185/65 R14, the figure 14 is the
questions.explanation: 185 is width in mm, 65 is the aspect ratio (%), R radial and 14 the rim diameter in inches.

questions.stem: Steering wheel shake that gets worse at about 80 to 100 km/h is MOST likely caused by
questions.explanation: Wheel imbalance gives vibration that peaks in a particular speed range; wheel balancing cures it.

questions.stem: Hydraulic brakes work on the principle that pressure in an enclosed liquid is
options: lost at every bend in the pipe
greater at the master cylinder only
zero when the pedal is pressed
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle: pressure applied at the master cylinder is transmitted equally to every wheel cylinder.

questions.stem: A brake pedal that feels spongy and goes down further than normal usually means
options: there is air in the hydraulic system
questions.explanation: Air is compressible, so it makes the pedal soft; the system must be bled.

questions.stem: An advantage of disc brakes over drum brakes is that disc brakes
options: are cheaper to make in every case
dissipate heat better and so resist fade
questions.explanation: The exposed disc cools quickly, so it resists fade; drums have self-servo action but fade more.

questions.stem: Front wheels that are closer together at the front than at the rear are said to have
questions.explanation: Toe-in means the fronts of the wheels point slightly towards each other.

questions.stem: The backward tilt of the steering axis that gives self-centring of the steering is called
questions.explanation: Positive castor puts the contact patch behind the steering axis, giving a self-centring trail effect.

questions.stem: A car keeps bouncing several times after passing over a speed bump. The part most likely to be faulty is the
questions.explanation: Dampers absorb spring oscillation; a worn damper lets the body keep bouncing.

questions.stem: A 3 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 4 Ω and 12 Ω resistors across a 12 V supply. The current from the supply is
questions.explanation: Parallel pair = 4 x 12/16 = 3 Ω; total = 6 Ω; I = 12/6 = 2 A.

questions.stem: Cables in a vehicle loom are colour coded so that
options: each circuit can be traced easily
questions.explanation: Colour codes identify circuits on the wiring diagram, making fault finding easier.

questions.stem: Only distilled water, not tap water, should be used to top up a lead-acid battery because tap water
options: is too heavy to mix with acid
contains impurities that damage the plates
makes the battery give a higher voltage
removes the need for a charger
questions.explanation: Minerals and chlorine in tap water contaminate the electrolyte and plates and increase self-discharge.

questions.stem: A major advantage of the alternator over the dynamo is that the alternator
options: has a heavy commutator that lasts longer
gives useful output even at engine idling speed
can be used as a starter
questions.explanation: An alternator charges well at low engine speed and is lighter; a dynamo gives little output at idle.

questions.stem: On a dashboard, a small device that glows when current passes through it in the forward direction and uses very little power is a(n)
questions.explanation: A light-emitting diode emits light when forward biased and draws little current.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes a multi-point arrangement?
options: one injector in the throttle body for all cylinders
one injector for each cylinder in the inlet port
questions.explanation: Multi-point systems have one injector per cylinder spraying towards the inlet valve; single-point uses one injector in the throttle body.

questions.stem: In a car air-conditioning system, the component in front of the radiator that gives out the heat removed from the cabin is the
questions.explanation: Hot high-pressure refrigerant from the compressor gives up heat and condenses in the condenser at the front of the car.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the four strokes of a four-stroke diesel engine. [8 marks]
(b) State three advantages and two disadvantages of the diesel engine compared with the petrol engine. [5 marks]
(c) Give two reasons for decarbonising a cylinder head. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) induction: inlet valve open, piston descends, only air drawn in
2 marks: (a) compression: valves closed, air compressed to high pressure and temperature (CR about 16–22:1)
2 marks: (a) power: fuel injected near TDC, ignites by heat of compression, gases force piston down
2 marks: (a) exhaust: exhaust valve open, piston rises expelling burnt gases
3 marks: (b) advantages any three: better fuel economy, more torque, cheaper fuel (in some markets), longer life, no ignition system (1 each)
2 marks: (b) disadvantages any two: heavier, noisier, more expensive to build, harder cold starting (1 each)
2 marks: (c) carbon deposits cause pre-ignition/raise compression, cause poor valve seating and loss of power (any two, 1 each)
questions.explanation: Diesel: induction of air, compression to high temperature, injection and self-ignition giving power, exhaust. It is economical and durable but heavy, noisy and costly. Decarbonising removes deposits that cause pinking, hot spots and poor valve seating.

questions.stem:
(a) With reference to a simple carburettor, explain the functions of the float chamber, the venturi and the throttle valve. [6 marks]
(b) State three merits and two demerits of petrol injection compared with a carburettor. [5 marks]
(c) Describe one cold-starting device used on petrol engines. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) float chamber: keeps constant fuel level using float and needle valve
2 marks: (a) venturi: narrow throat increases air speed and lowers pressure so fuel is drawn from jet
2 marks: (a) throttle: butterfly valve controlling quantity of mixture, hence engine speed/power
3 marks: (b) merits any three: accurate metering, better economy, lower emissions, better cold starts, more power (1 each)
2 marks: (b) demerits any two: costly, complex, needs special diagnostic tools, sensitive to dirty fuel (1 each)
4 marks: (c) choke/strangler: valve above venturi closed to reduce air and give rich mixture for cold start; opens as engine warms (or auto-choke/cold-start injector described)
questions.explanation: Float chamber keeps level, venturi creates depression to draw fuel, throttle controls flow. Injection meters accurately and cleanly but is costly and complex. A choke restricts air to enrich the mixture for cold starts.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four main components of a pump-assisted water cooling system and state the function of each. [8 marks]
(b) Explain the difference between thermo-syphon and pump-assisted circulation. [4 marks]
(c) State three causes of engine overheating. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) radiator: transfers heat from coolant to air
2 marks: (a) water pump: circulates coolant
2 marks: (a) thermostat: controls coolant flow to give quick warm-up
2 marks: (a) fan/hoses/pressure cap: draws air through radiator / carry coolant / raises boiling point (any one)
2 marks: (b) thermo-syphon: circulation by natural convection, hot water rises, cool water sinks; needs large passages
2 marks: (b) pump-assisted: pump forces circulation, faster flow, smaller radiator possible
3 marks: (c) any three: low coolant, slipping/broken fan belt, stuck thermostat, blocked radiator, faulty pump, retarded timing (1 each)
questions.explanation: Radiator, pump, thermostat and fan/hoses form the system. Thermo-syphon relies on convection; pump-assisted forces flow. Overheating arises from low coolant, belt faults, thermostats, blocked radiators or pump failure.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the operation of a synchromesh unit when changing gear. [6 marks]
(b) A vehicle has a first gear ratio of 3.5 : 1 and a final drive ratio of 4.2 : 1. Calculate (i) the overall gear ratio, (ii) the road wheel speed when the engine runs at 2940 rev/min in first gear. [5 marks]
(c) State two functions of the universal joint and two of the sliding joint on a propeller shaft. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) gear lever moves synchro hub/sleeve towards the gear; cone of baulk ring contacts cone on gear
2 marks: (a) friction between cones equalises speeds of gear and mainshaft
2 marks: (a) when speeds equal, sleeve slides over dog teeth to lock gear to shaft, giving silent change
2 marks: (b)(i) overall ratio = 3.5 x 4.2 = 14.7 : 1
3 marks: (b)(ii) wheel speed = 2940/14.7 = 200 rev/min
2 marks: (c) universal joint: transmits drive through a changing angle as axle moves (2 points/1 each)
2 marks: (c) sliding joint: allows change in shaft length with suspension movement; allows assembly (1 each)
questions.explanation: Synchromesh cones use friction to match speeds before the dog teeth engage. Overall ratio 3.5 x 4.2 = 14.7; wheel speed 2940/14.7 = 200 rev/min. Universal joints accommodate angle changes; sliding joints accommodate length changes.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe how a hydraulic drum brake system works from the pedal to the shoes. [6 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for bleeding a hydraulic brake system. [5 marks]
(c) State four faults that may cause a vehicle to pull to one side when braking. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) pedal pushes master cylinder piston creating fluid pressure
2 marks: (a) pressure transmitted through pipes equally to wheel cylinders
2 marks: (a) wheel cylinder pistons push shoes against drum; return springs retract shoes on release
1 mark: (b) top up reservoir
1 mark: (b) fit tube on bleed nipple of wheel furthest from master cylinder, end in jar of fluid
1 mark: (b) assistant pumps and holds pedal; open nipple
1 mark: (b) close nipple before pedal released; repeat until no bubbles
1 mark: (b) repeat at other wheels, keep reservoir topped up
4 marks: (c) any four: oil/grease on linings, seized wheel cylinder, unequal tyre pressures, wrong adjustment, worn linings on one side, loose suspension/steering parts (1 each)
questions.explanation: Pedal force creates pressure in the master cylinder which is transmitted to wheel cylinders to expand the shoes. Bleed from the furthest wheel, pumping and closing nipple until no bubbles. Pulling results from contaminated linings, seized cylinders, unequal pressures or adjustment.

questions.stem:
(a) State five main causes of road accidents in Nigeria. [5 marks]
(b) List five essentials of safe driving. [5 marks]
(c) Name five safety devices fitted to modern vehicles. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) any five: over-speeding, drunk driving, bad roads, poor vehicle maintenance, dangerous overtaking, fatigue, phone use while driving, ignoring road signs (1 each)
5 marks: (b) any five: obey highway code, keep safe distance, check vehicle before trip, wear seat belt, avoid alcohol, rest when tired, use indicators (1 each)
5 marks: (c) any five: seat belts, airbags, ABS, head restraints, crumple zones, side-impact bars, warning triangle, fire extinguisher (1 each)
questions.explanation: Accidents come from speeding, drink-driving, bad roads, poor maintenance, fatigue and distraction. Safe driving means obeying the code, keeping distance, checking the vehicle and staying sober. Safety devices include seat belts, airbags, ABS and crumple zones.
